comp-database.blockPlan:
Give this module 20-25 minutes a day inside your 4-hour block, placed in a low-concentration slot — abbreviations revise perfectly well while tired, whereas puzzles do not. Never let it eat morning reasoning time.
WEEK 1 — Day 1: 45 minutes, handwrite Sheet A (database concepts, all five blocks). Day 2: 50 minutes, handwrite Sheet B (abbreviations in six families, about 90 entries). These two sittings are the only long ones this topic ever gets. Day 3-6: 20 minutes daily = 5 minutes on one Sheet A block, 5 minutes on one Sheet B family, 10 minutes on 20 practice questions. Day 7: 25-minute full revision plus the first timed drill (40 abbreviations in 6 minutes, 10 database prompts in 3 minutes).
WEEK 2-3 — 15 minutes daily: 4 minutes Sheet B (rotate families, and every third day do the harder reverse direction, expansion to abbreviation), 4 minutes one Sheet A block, 7 minutes of mixed questions. Sunday: timed drill plus a 40-question mixed computer set. Every miss goes on the error strip.
WEEK 4 ONWARDS — maintenance: Sheet B for 4 minutes on alternate days (abbreviations decay faster than concepts and need more frequent contact), Sheet A twice a week for 8 minutes, one Sunday drill. Fold both into the same daily slot as General Awareness current-affairs revision since all three are recall subjects on the same spaced-repetition rhythm.
LAST 10 DAYS BEFORE 27 DECEMBER — error strip only, 5 minutes a day. Do not add new abbreviations in December; late additions interfere with items already consolidated.
MOCK RULE: in every Reasoning & Computer Aptitude sectional, sweep the paper for computer questions first, clear them in under 90 seconds, and only then open the puzzle sets. If a computer question crosses 20 seconds in a mock, mark it and add it to the error strip that evening — the diagnosis is a memory gap, never a technique gap.

comp-banking.topicName: Computing in Banking: CBS, Payment Systems and RBI Digital Rules
comp-banking.whatItIs: The banking-flavoured half of Computer Awareness, and the block where IBPS overlaps this section with General and Banking Awareness. It covers Core Banking Solution, the five retail payment rails (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, AePS) and NACH, and exactly how they differ in operator, settlement mechanism, timing and limits; the delivery channels (ATM and its white/brown-label and micro-ATM variants, POS terminals, NFS); cheque infrastructure (Cheque Truncation System, CTS-2010 standard, Positive Pay, MICR and IFSC code structure); card tokenisation and the RBI card-data storage rule; digital wallets and Prepaid Payment Instruments; NPCI's product family; and the handful of RBI customer-protection rules an aspirant is expected to know. Every item is a number or a definition. There is no derivation — the mark turns on whether you have the figure, and figures are what candidates get wrong.
comp-banking.coreMethod:
1. Build ONE A4 sheet, both sides, and treat the numbers on it as sacred — this is the only Computer Awareness sheet where a stale figure actively loses you marks.
2. SIDE 1, THE MASTER TABLE — draw six columns (SYSTEM | RUN BY | SETTLEMENT | TIMING | MINIMUM | MAXIMUM) and fill six rows. NEFT: RBI; deferred NET settlement in half-hourly batches (48 batches a day); 24x7x365 since 16 December 2019; minimum ₹1; no RBI-set maximum (banks fix their own caps); RBI has waived charges on online NEFT from savings accounts. RTGS: RBI; REAL-TIME GROSS settlement, transaction by transaction; 24x7x365 since 14 December 2020; minimum ₹2,00,000; no upper limit. IMPS: NPCI; instant, interbank; 24x7x365 since 2010; NPCI ceiling ₹5,00,000 per transaction; works with account number plus IFSC, or with mobile number plus MMID. UPI: NPCI; instant; 24x7x365; launched 2016; standard cap ₹1,00,000 per transaction, with ₹5,00,000 per transaction for verified merchants in specified categories — insurance, capital markets, travel, collections, GeM including tax payments, with a ₹10,00,000 daily aggregate, and credit-card bill payments at ₹5,00,000 per transaction and ₹6,00,000 a day — effective 15 September 2025; person-to-person transfers remain at ₹1,00,000 a day. Add UPI Lite: on-device wallet, no UPI PIN, ₹1,000 per transaction, ₹5,000 maximum balance, ₹10,000 a day; and UPI 123Pay for feature phones, limit ₹10,000. AePS: NPCI; Aadhaar number plus bank name (IIN) plus fingerprint or iris, through a Business Correspondent on a micro-ATM; no card, no PIN, no signature; services are cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement and Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar fund transfer, plus eKYC and Best Finger Detection. NACH: NPCI; BULK and repetitive; replaced the older regional ECS; NACH Credit pays salary, pension, dividend and DBT subsidy; NACH Debit collects EMI, SIP, insurance premium and utility bills against a mandate or e-mandate.
3. SIDE 1, LOWER BLOCK — CBS in four lines: Core Banking Solution, sometimes expanded as Centralised Online Real-time Exchange; a single centralised database so a customer belongs to the bank rather than to a branch; enables anywhere-banking, a unique Customer ID (CIF), and real-time posting; common software includes Finacle, TCS BaNCS and Oracle FLEXCUBE.
4. SIDE 2, CHEQUE BLOCK — CTS: Cheque Truncation System, an RBI system launched 2010, in which the physical cheque stops at the presenting bank and only the IMAGE plus the MICR data travel electronically; CTS-2010 is the mandatory cheque-paper standard; the whole country now runs on a single grid. Current change worth knowing: RBI has moved CTS from batch processing to CONTINUOUS clearing with settlement on realisation, Phase 1 from 4 October 2025 (same-day credit, presentation window 10:00 to 16:00, confirmation by 19:00) and Phase 2 from 3 January 2026 (confirmation within T+3 hours, hourly settlement). Positive Pay System: from 1 January 2021, the issuer re-confirms cheque details electronically; banks must enable it for cheques of ₹50,000 and above and MAY make it compulsory for ₹5,00,000 and above.
5. SIDE 2, CODE BLOCK — MICR: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition, printed in E-13B font at the bottom of the cheque, 9 DIGITS in three parts of three — City (matching the first three digits of the PIN code) + Bank + Branch. IFSC: Indian Financial System Code, 11 CHARACTERS — first 4 alphabetic (bank), 5th always ZERO (reserved for future use), last 6 alphanumeric (branch); used for NEFT, RTGS and IMPS. SWIFT/BIC: 8 or 11 characters, for international transfers. Write the pair 'MICR = 9 digits, cheque clearing; IFSC = 11 characters, fund transfer' as one line.
6. SIDE 2, CARDS AND WALLETS — Tokenisation: the actual 16-digit card number is replaced by a device-and-merchant-specific TOKEN; since 1 January 2022 no entity in the card payment chain other than the card ISSUER and the card NETWORK may store actual card data, so merchants and payment aggregators must purge it; tokenisation is free, needs explicit customer consent with Additional Factor of Authentication, and Card-on-File Tokenisation can now also be done through the issuing bank's net banking or mobile app. PPIs (Prepaid Payment Instruments) come in three kinds — closed (usable only with the issuer), semi-closed (a group of merchants, no cash withdrawal) and open (issued only by banks, usable anywhere including ATM withdrawal); full-KYC PPIs may hold up to ₹2,00,000 outstanding and are UPI-interoperable, while minimum-detail small PPIs are capped at ₹10,000 loading per month and ₹1,20,000 a year. Note that RBI issued a DRAFT Master Direction on PPIs in April 2026 which is not yet the operative rule.
7. SIDE 2, ATM/POS AND NPCI BLOCK — ATM types: onsite, offsite, White Label (owned and operated by a non-bank company), Brown Label (hardware owned by a third party while cash and connectivity are the bank's), Micro ATM (handheld, used by Business Correspondents, biometric), Cash Recycler (accepts and dispenses). NFS, the National Financial Switch, is NPCI's ATM network. POS = Point of Sale terminal at the merchant; mPOS is its mobile form. Free ATM transactions: 5 a month at your own bank's ATMs and, at other banks' ATMs, 3 in metro and 5 in non-metro centres, all counts including non-financial transactions; beyond that a bank may charge up to ₹23 per transaction plus tax, effective 1 May 2025 (raised from ₹21); interchange is ₹17 financial and ₹6 non-financial. NPCI product list to memorise as one string: UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS, NACH, NFS, BHIM, NETC FASTag, BBPS, *99# USSD, Bharat QR.
8. REVISION RHYTHM: read the sheet on Day 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 30 then weekly. Because the figures are the examinable content, one session a month must be a VERIFICATION pass — open rbi.org.in and npci.org.in and re-check the UPI limits, ATM charges, PPI caps and CTS timings, then correct the sheet in a different colour. Do this in early November and again in the second week of December.
9. SELF-TEST BY REVERSAL: cover the SYSTEM column and read only a settlement description or a limit, then name the rail. The exam gives you the property, not the name.
10. NUMBER STRIP: copy every figure — ₹2 lakh, ₹5 lakh, ₹1 lakh, ₹1,000/₹5,000/₹10,000, 9 digits, 11 characters, ₹50,000, ₹23, 5/3/5 — onto a separate slip. Numbers are what get confused, and the slip is your final week's revision.
11. SUNDAY TIMED DRILL: 20 mixed banking-technology prompts in 5 minutes. Anything over 15 seconds goes on the number strip.
tricks: ONE LETTER TELLS THE SETTLEMENT: RTGS has the G for GROSS — each transaction settled individually and instantly; NEFT is settled NET in half-hourly batches. If a question describes 'settled in batches', it is NEFT; 'individually and in real time', it is RTGS.

THE ₹2 LAKH FLOOR belongs to RTGS and to nothing else. RTGS is the only Indian retail rail with a MINIMUM — memorise it as 'RTGS starts at 2 lakh and has no ceiling', which is the exact inverse of UPI's 'starts at 1 rupee and stops at 1 lakh'.

OPERATOR SPLIT in one line: RBI runs NEFT and RTGS; NPCI runs everything else — IMPS, UPI, AePS, NACH, RuPay, NFS, BHIM, FASTag, BBPS. Two for RBI, the rest for NPCI. This alone answers a whole family of questions.

AePS = AADHAAR ONLY. No card, no PIN, no signature, no cheque — the identifiers are the Aadhaar number, the bank's name (IIN) and a fingerprint or iris. If an option mentions a debit card or a PIN in an AePS question, it is wrong by construction.

CODE LENGTHS as a rhyme: 'MICR nine on the cheque line, IFSC eleven for transfer heaven.' Then the internal splits: MICR 3+3+3 = City, Bank, Branch; IFSC 4 letters + a zero + 6 characters = Bank, reserved, Branch. The FIFTH character of an IFSC is always zero — that single fact is asked directly.

TRUNCATION MEANS THE PAPER STOPS. 'Truncate' = cut short: in CTS the physical cheque's journey is cut short at the presenting bank and only its image plus MICR data travel onward. That image sentence answers every definitional CTS question.

TOKEN = A STAND-IN, NOT A COPY. The token replaces the card number and is specific to one device and one merchant, so a leak from one merchant is useless elsewhere. Since 1 January 2022 only the card ISSUER and the card NETWORK may store real card data — remember 'issuer and network keep it, everyone else deletes it'.

PPI COLOUR-CODE by reach: CLOSED = closed inside one company, no cash out; SEMI-CLOSED = a group of merchants, still no cash out; OPEN = open everywhere including ATM cash withdrawal, and only BANKS may issue open PPIs. The word in the name is the answer.

NACH DIRECTION: NACH Credit pushes money OUT of an institution to many people (salary, pension, dividend, DBT subsidy); NACH Debit pulls money IN from many people (EMI, SIP, insurance premium, utility bills). Ask 'who is being paid?' and the direction is settled.

WHITE vs BROWN LABEL ATM by who owns what: WHITE = a non-bank company owns and runs the whole thing (a fully non-bank ATM). BROWN = a mixed arrangement, third party owns the hardware while the bank supplies the cash, the branding and the connectivity — brown is a mixed colour, and this is the mixed model.
traps: NEFT vs RTGS MINIMUM: RTGS has a minimum of ₹2 lakh; NEFT has a minimum of ₹1. Candidates reverse these or invent a NEFT maximum — RBI sets no NEFT ceiling, though individual banks cap their own channels.

NEFT vs RTGS SETTLEMENT: NEFT settles in half-hourly BATCHES (deferred net settlement), RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time. Both are now 24x7x365, so timing no longer separates them — only the settlement mechanism and the ₹2 lakh floor do. Options claiming NEFT works 'only on working days' are stale and wrong.

IMPS vs UPI CEILING: the NPCI standard IMPS ceiling is ₹5 lakh per transaction; the standard UPI cap is ₹1 lakh per transaction, with ₹5 lakh only for verified merchants in specified categories such as insurance, capital markets, travel, collections and GeM. Do not apply the ₹5 lakh figure to ordinary person-to-person UPI, which remains ₹1 lakh.

UPI vs UPI LITE: UPI Lite is an on-device wallet needing NO UPI PIN, capped at ₹1,000 per transaction with a ₹5,000 balance and ₹10,000 a day. Candidates apply the main UPI ₹1 lakh figure to Lite, or claim Lite needs a PIN.
RBI vs NPCI OWNERSHIP: NEFT and RTGS are RBI systems; IMPS, UPI, AePS, NACH, RuPay, NFS, BHIM, NETC FASTag and BBPS are NPCI's. Attributing UPI to RBI is the single most common error in this module.

MICR vs IFSC vs SWIFT: MICR is 9 DIGITS and is for cheque clearing; IFSC is 11 CHARACTERS and is for electronic fund transfer within India; SWIFT/BIC is 8 or 11 characters and is for international transfers. All three appear in the same option set, and the digit counts are what the question turns on.

IFSC FIFTH CHARACTER: it is always the numeral ZERO, reserved for future use — not a letter, and not part of the branch code. Options offering 'the fifth character denotes the state' or 'the city' are distractors.
MICR PART ORDER: City first, then Bank, then Branch — 3+3+3. Reversing bank and city, or claiming MICR is 11 digits, are the planted errors.

AePS vs MICRO-ATM vs POS: AePS is the Aadhaar-and-biometric SERVICE; the micro-ATM is the handheld DEVICE the Business Correspondent uses to deliver it; a POS terminal is the merchant's card machine. The question may describe the device and ask for the service, or the reverse.
NACH vs ECS: NACH is NPCI's national system that replaced the older, regional and slower ECS. Treating them as the same system, or calling ECS the newer one, loses the mark.

CTS MISCONCEPTION: under CTS the physical cheque is NOT sent to the drawee bank — only the image and the MICR data are transmitted. Also, cheque clearing is no longer a T+1 batch process: RBI moved CTS to continuous clearing with settlement on realisation from 4 October 2025, with hourly settlement and T+3-hour confirmation from 3 January 2026. Any option describing a two-day clearing cycle is stale.

POSITIVE PAY THRESHOLDS: banks must ENABLE it for cheques of ₹50,000 and above, and MAY make it MANDATORY at ₹5,00,000 and above. The two figures pair with two different verbs, and swapping them is the trap.

TOKENISATION SCOPE: tokenisation does not encrypt your card — it substitutes a different number. It is free, requires customer consent with Additional Factor of Authentication, and produces a token tied to one merchant and one device. The rule that only issuers and card networks may store actual card data has applied since 1 January 2022.

PPI BALANCE CAPS: full-KYC PPI outstanding balance up to ₹2,00,000; minimum-detail small PPI loading capped at ₹10,000 per month and ₹1,20,000 per year. Note that only banks may issue OPEN system PPIs permitting cash withdrawal — non-bank wallets cannot.

ATM FREE-TRANSACTION COUNTS: 5 free at your own bank's ATMs, and at other banks' ATMs 3 free in METRO and 5 free in NON-METRO centres — the metro figure is the smaller one, which candidates reverse. The counts include non-financial transactions such as balance enquiry, and the charge beyond the free limit is up to ₹23 plus tax from 1 May 2025.
comp-banking.timeTarget: 12-20 seconds, the longest allowance in Computer Awareness because these stems are wordier and often embed a scenario. Read the stem, identify which rail or which code is being described, then match. If the figure does not come back within 20 seconds, leave it — with five options and 0.25 negative, a half-remembered limit is worse than a blank. Budget for the whole 5-question computer block: under 90 seconds out of your 35 minutes.
comp-banking.masteryCheck: You own this module when you can, from a blank page and timed, (a) reproduce the six-row master table — operator, settlement, timing, minimum and maximum for NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, AePS and NACH — in under 5 minutes with every figure correct; (b) state MICR and IFSC lengths and their internal splits, including that the fifth IFSC character is zero, in under 20 seconds; (c) give the two Positive Pay thresholds with the correct verb attached to each, the tokenisation storage rule and its effective date, and the ATM free-transaction counts, without hesitation; and (d) score 18 or better on 20 mixed prompts in 5 minutes. One additional non-negotiable condition: your sheet must have been verified against rbi.org.in and npci.org.in within the last 30 days, because a perfectly memorised stale number is still a wrong answer.
questionPatterns: Q: What is the minimum amount that can be remitted through RTGS? (a) ₹1 (b) ₹10,000 (c) ₹1,00,000 (d) ₹2,00,000 (e) There is no minimum limit — ANSWER: (d) ₹2,00,000. RTGS has a minimum but no maximum; NEFT has a minimum of ₹1 and no RBI-prescribed maximum.

Q: Which of the following payment systems settles transactions on a deferred net basis in half-hourly batches rather than individually in real time? (a) RTGS (b) NEFT (c) IMPS (d) UPI (e) AePS — ANSWER: (b) NEFT.

Q: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is owned and operated by — (a) Reserve Bank of India (b) Ministry of Finance (c) National Payments Corporation of India (d) Indian Banks' Association (e) State Bank of India — ANSWER: (c) NPCI. RBI operates NEFT and RTGS; NPCI operates UPI, IMPS, AePS, NACH, RuPay and BHIM.

Q: An Indian Financial System Code (IFSC) consists of 11 characters. The fifth character of an IFSC is — (a) always the letter A (b) always the numeral 0 (c) a letter denoting the state (d) a digit denoting the city (e) the first letter of the branch name — ANSWER: (b) always the numeral zero, reserved for future use.

Q: The MICR code printed at the bottom of a cheque consists of how many digits, and in what order are its three parts arranged? (a) 9 digits — Bank, City, Branch (b) 9 digits — City, Bank, Branch (c) 11 digits — City, Bank, Branch (d) 9 digits — Branch, Bank, City (e) 11 characters — Bank, zero, Branch — ANSWER: (b) 9 digits arranged as City, Bank, Branch.

Q: Under the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS), a customer at a Business Correspondent's micro-ATM must provide — (a) debit card and PIN (b) cheque and signature (c) Aadhaar number, bank name and biometric authentication (d) passbook and PAN card (e) UPI PIN and mobile number — ANSWER: (c). AePS uses no card, no PIN and no signature.

Q: Under the Cheque Truncation System (CTS), what is sent from the presenting bank to the drawee bank? (a) The original physical cheque by courier (b) Only a telephonic confirmation (c) The electronic image of the cheque along with its MICR data (d) A photocopy of the cheque by post (e) Only the account number and amount by SMS — ANSWER: (c). The physical cheque's movement is truncated at the presenting bank.

Q: As per RBI's Positive Pay System for CTS, banks are required to enable the facility for cheques of which value and above? (a) ₹10,000 (b) ₹25,000 (c) ₹50,000 (d) ₹1,00,000 (e) ₹5,00,000 — ANSWER: (c) ₹50,000. Banks MAY additionally make it mandatory for cheques of ₹5,00,000 and above.

Q: In card tokenisation as mandated by RBI, which entities are permitted to store the actual card details? (a) Merchants and payment aggregators only (b) Card issuers and card networks only (c) Any entity holding customer consent (d) Payment gateways and merchants (e) Only the customer's mobile wallet provider — ANSWER: (b). Since 1 January 2022 no other entity in the card payment chain may store actual card data.

Q: Which of the following is NOT a product or service of the National Payments Corporation of India? (a) RuPay (b) BHIM (c) NETC FASTag (d) RTGS (e) Bharat Bill Payment System — ANSWER: (d) RTGS, which is operated by the Reserve Bank of India.

Q: A customer may make a maximum of how many free transactions in a month at ATMs of banks OTHER than his own, located in a metro centre? (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 4 (d) 5 (e) 6 — ANSWER: (b) 3 in metro centres, against 5 in non-metro centres and 5 at one's own bank's ATMs; the counts include non-financial transactions.

comp-banking.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk Mains paper setter for the Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude section. Generate 20 questions on computing in banking. EVERY question must have exactly FIVE options labelled (a) to (e) — IBPS papers have five options, never four. Cover: 6 questions distinguishing NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI and AePS by operator, settlement mechanism, minimum and maximum, including at least one on the ₹2 lakh RTGS minimum and one on NEFT's batch settlement; 2 on NACH credit versus NACH debit and how NACH differs from the older ECS; 2 on Core Banking Solution and what it enables; 3 on cheque infrastructure — CTS and what actually travels between banks, the CTS-2010 standard, and the Positive Pay thresholds; 2 on code structure, one on MICR's 9 digits and city-bank-branch order and one on IFSC's 11 characters with a zero as the fifth; 2 on card tokenisation and which entities may store actual card data; 1 on PPI categories and the full-KYC balance cap; and 2 on ATM types (white label, brown label, micro-ATM) and POS terminals. Use these verified 2026 facts and do not alter them: NEFT and RTGS are RBI systems and both run 24x7x365; IMPS, UPI, AePS, NACH, RuPay, NFS, BHIM, NETC FASTag and BBPS are NPCI's; the NPCI IMPS ceiling is ₹5 lakh per transaction; the standard UPI cap is ₹1 lakh per transaction with ₹5 lakh for verified merchants in specified categories effective 15 September 2025; UPI Lite is ₹1,000 per transaction with a ₹5,000 balance; only card issuers and card networks may store actual card data, in force since 1 January 2022; RBI moved CTS to continuous clearing from 4 October 2025 with hourly settlement from 3 January 2026. Make the distractors the neighbouring rail or the neighbouring figure, never an absurd number. Provide an answer key with a one-line reason for each. Do not invent any limit, date or percentage — if you are unsure of a figure, write the question so it does not depend on that figure.
comp-banking.blockPlan:
Give this module 20-25 minutes a day, and place it in the same slot as your Banking Awareness reading, because roughly half of this sheet also earns marks in the General/Financial Awareness section — it is the highest cross-yield content in the syllabus.
WEEK 1 — Day 1: 60 minutes, handwrite Side 1 (the six-row master table plus CBS). Day 2: 50 minutes, handwrite Side 2 (cheques, codes, cards, wallets, ATM/POS, NPCI list). Day 3-6: 20 minutes daily = 8 minutes on one block, 12 minutes on 15 practice questions. Day 7: 25-minute full revision plus the first timed drill (20 prompts, 5 minutes).
WEEK 2-3 — 15 minutes daily: 5 minutes on the number strip (every figure on the sheet, drilled as bare numbers), 10 minutes of mixed questions from your bank. Sunday: timed drill plus a 40-question mixed computer set. Every miss goes on the number strip.
WEEK 4 ONWARDS — maintenance twice a week, 10 minutes, plus one Sunday drill.
TWO MANDATORY VERIFICATION PASSES — one in early November and one in the second week of December: sit with rbi.org.in and npci.org.in and re-check the UPI caps, ATM charge and free-transaction counts, PPI limits, Positive Pay thresholds and CTS clearing timings, then correct the sheet in red ink. Payment-system numbers change more often than any other content in Clerk Mains, and a confidently memorised obsolete figure costs you the mark AND 0.25 on top — in a section averaging 1.5 marks a question, that is close to a two-mark swing. Note in particular that RBI issued a DRAFT Master Direction on PPIs in April 2026 — check before the exam whether it has become operative, and until it does, answer from the existing framework.
LAST 10 DAYS BEFORE 27 DECEMBER — number strip only, 5 minutes daily, alongside your banking current-affairs revision.
MOCK RULE: clear the computer questions in the first 90 seconds of every Reasoning & Computer Aptitude sectional, then start the puzzles. These questions exist to fund your puzzle time.
